content:
ash: Quick flag from kitsune-v1 int6 bringup: vertical Han/Hanja translation BLEU dropped vs fp16. Baseline fp16 BLEU=31.9 -> kitsune-int6 BLEU=27.4 on our vertical test split. Also seeing bracket mirroring on RTL fragments in mixed-orient examples.

maria: paste eval command + raw metrics?

ash: ran on ci-evals: 
```
python tools/eval_translate.py --model=kitsune-v1:quant=int6 --testset=data/vertical_hanja_mixed_orient.jsonl --metrics=bleu,chrf --batch=48
```
raw: kitsune-int6 BLEU=27.4 chrF=43.9 | baseline-fp16 BLEU=31.9 chrF=49.1. eval-bot: diff BLEU=-4.5 (p<0.01).

li: short failing example? tokenization seems suspect.

ash: sample:
src: " \u6f22\u5b57(注)"
ref: "...\u6f22\u5b57(注) 参照"
kitsune-int6: "...\u6f22\u5b57(注) 参照" but in several cases parentheses content duplicated or punctuation moved to opposite side when Arabic segments present.

maria: looks like detokenizer merge + bidi postprocessing order might have flipped. token_map used for quant build unchanged. runtime detok optimization intentionally merges adjacent punctuation to save tokens.

jong: i've added a tiny human-inspect set to ci/regress/vertical_hanja_manual.jsonl (PR #3567). also ran a chrF-focused subset.

ash: bisect plan: (1) int6 kernels with original detok; (2) int6 + detok-merge-off; (3) int6 + kvcache-timing-old. will post hashes and small diffs. ETA ~90m.

li: i'll grep for zenkaku/ideograph punctuation handlers and check bidi anchoring ordering in detok.

maria: if detok merge is culprit, short-term mitigation: gate merge on locale/orientation and disable for mixed-orient samples. tagging: P0 if regression persists for onboard.

eval-bot: smoke subset run queued.

(END)
